answer_text: Yes, by its own account. Todoist says an attacker used a stolen credential to get into its systems on Nov 23 and took email addresses and old password hashes for about 6% of users. Smaller groups lost tokens, task text or email previews.
label: Confirmed

answer_text: Not the passwords themselves. For about 6% of users the attacker took password hashes stored the old way, which can be open to guessing. Todoist has disabled those passwords; affected users should reset theirs and change it where reused.
label: Confirmed

answer_text: Todoist says affected users have been emailed and should follow that email; anyone who did not get one need do nothing. It warns users to watch for fake emails about the incident.
label: Reported

question_text: How did the attacker get the first credential?
what_would_settle_it: Todoist or outside investigators explaining how the version control credential was stolen.

question_text: How many Todoist accounts were affected?
what_would_settle_it: Todoist giving a number of accounts rather than a share of users.

question_text: Who was behind the Todoist breach?
what_would_settle_it: Todoist, law enforcement or a credible independent analysis naming the attacker.

question_text: Have regulators or police been told about the Todoist breach?
what_would_settle_it: Todoist or a regulator saying that the breach has been reported to them.
